original_body_unit:
- **Most common entity type** — Limited Liability Company (LLC)  _(Commercial Companies Law (Royal Decree No. 18/2019) — https://www.sovereigngroup.com/news/how-to-set-up-an-llc-in-oman/)_
- **Other entity types** — One Person Company (OPC/SPC), joint stock company (SAOC closed / SAOG public), partnership, joint venture, branch of a foreign company, and holding company  _(Commercial Companies Law (Royal Decree No. 18/2019) — https://mawaleh.com/blog/llc-formation/)_
- **Foreign ownership** — 100% foreign ownership permitted for most activities (subject to a restricted/negative list)  _(Foreign Capital Investment Law (Royal Decree No. 50/2019) — https://gulfcoreservices.com/blog/how-to-form-a-100-foreign-owned-company-in-oman-rules-fees-and-timeline/)_
- **Minimum share capital (LLC, general)** — No statutory minimum for most activities; capital should be adequate for the activity ((approx — confirm by activity))  _(Foreign Capital Investment Law (Royal Decree No. 50/2019) — https://omanbss.com/what-is-the-minimum-capital-for-llc-in-oman/)_
- **Minimum capital often required in practice (foreign-owned)** — OMR 150,000 is commonly applied for foreign-owned LLCs in certain/regulated activities OMR ((approx — confirm; varies by activity and free-zone status)) OMR  _(Foreign Capital Investment Law (Royal Decree No. 50/2019) — https://www.sovereigngroup.com/news/how-to-set-up-an-llc-in-oman/)_
- **Number of shareholders (LLC)** — 1 (One Person Company) to a statutory maximum; typically 2 or more for a standard LLC ((approx — confirm statutory maximum))  _(Commercial Companies Law (Royal Decree No. 18/2019) — https://mawaleh.com/blog/llc-formation/)_
- **Registration authority** — Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MOCIIP) — Commercial Registration  _(Commercial Register Law / MOCIIP — https://intuitconsultancy.com/company-formation-in-oman/)_
- **Core incorporation steps** — Reserve company name (MOCIIP); draft and notarize Memorandum & Articles of Association; obtain security clearance for foreign investors where required; register for Commercial Registration; obtain municipality/activity licenses; register with the Tax Authority and SPF  _(Commercial Companies Law (Royal Decree No. 18/2019) — https://intuitconsultancy.com/company-formation-in-oman/)_
- **Typical incorporation timeline** — Approximately 2–3 weeks (name reservation 1–2 days; commercial registration and licensing ~5–10 business days) ((approx — varies by activity and clearances))  _(MOCIIP — https://www.gryffincapitalist.com/om)_
- **Core annual compliance** — Renew Commercial Registration; maintain accounting records and prepare financial statements; file annual corporate income tax return; file quarterly VAT returns (if registered); make monthly SPF contributions  _(Commercial Companies Law (Royal Decree No. 18/2019) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/oman/corporate/tax-administration)_
- **Statutory audit** — Audited financial statements are generally required for companies (joint stock companies and most LLCs of any size) ((approx — confirm exact thresholds/exemptions))  _(Commercial Companies Law (Royal Decree No. 18/2019) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/oman/corporate/tax-administration)_

original_section: Corporate income tax rates and base
original_body_unit:
- **Overview of corporate income tax** — Corporate income tax is Oman's principal direct tax, governed by the Income Tax Law. The standard rate is 15%, with a reduced 3% rate for qualifying Omani SMEs and a special 55% regime for petroleum income.  _(Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 28/2009))_
- **Standard corporate income tax rate** — 15 % (on taxable income)  _(Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 28/2009) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/oman/corporate/taxes-on-corporate-income)_
- **Reduced rate for qualifying SMEs** — 3 % (for Omani proprietorships/LLCs meeting SME conditions (registered with the authority for SME development; capital and turnover limits apply) (approx — confirm capital/turnover/headcount thresholds))  _(Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 28/2009) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/oman/corporate/taxes-on-corporate-income)_
- **Petroleum income tax rate** — 55 % (on income from the sale of petroleum (under specific EPSAs))  _(Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 28/2009) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/oman/corporate/taxes-on-corporate-income)_
- **Tax base** — Net taxable profit per the financial statements, adjusted for tax purposes; resident companies taxed on worldwide income  _(Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 28/2009) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/oman/corporate/income-determination)_
- **Standard withholding tax rate** — 10 % (on certain Oman-source payments to non-residents without a permanent establishment)  _(Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 28/2009) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/oman/corporate/withholding-taxes)_
- **Standard withholding tax rate** — 10 % (on certain Oman-source payments to non-residents without a permanent establishment)  _(Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 28/2009) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/oman/corporate/withholding-taxes)_
- **Standard withholding tax rate** — 10 % (on certain Oman-source payments to non-residents without a permanent establishment)  _(Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 28/2009) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/oman/corporate/withholding-taxes)_
- **Standard withholding tax rate** — 10 % (on certain Oman-source payments to non-residents without a permanent establishment)  _(Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 28/2009) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/oman/corporate/withholding-taxes)_
- **Withholding tax remittance deadline** — Within 14 days from the end of the month in which the payment was made  _(Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 28/2009) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/oman/corporate/withholding-taxes)_
- **Annual return and payment deadline** — Annual income tax return and payment due within 4 months of the accounting year-end (approx — confirm; some guides cite up to 6 months — verify against current Executive Regulations)  _(Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 28/2009) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/oman/corporate/tax-administration)_
- **Provisional return** — A provisional return is historically required early in the year (the formal two-stage filing has been streamlined under recent practice — confirm current requirement) (approx — confirm)  _(Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 28/2009) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/oman/corporate/tax-administration)_

original_body_unit: Accounts follow the accrual basis and international accounting standards (art. 12). Small enterprises use the cash basis unless the Authority approves another (art. 159bis 9 and following). Exempt: dividends from Omani companies and gains on securities listed in Muscat (art. 115). Shipping income of an Omani owner is exempt (art. 116). Losses carry forward for up to five years from the end of the loss year (art. 71); exempt activities cannot carry a loss (art. 72). Depreciation pools: 33 1/3% for machinery, computers, vehicles, fixtures and software; 10% for rigs; 15% for other plant (art. 90). Related-party transactions can be adjusted (art. 125). First accounting period: up to 18 months (art. 50). A register opened from January to June closes that 31 December; from July to December it closes the next 31 December (https://tms.taxoman.gov.om/portal/web/taxportal/income-tax-faqs, question 5).

original_body_unit:
- **Personal income tax for 2025** — None — individuals pay no tax on salaries, wages or other personal income; no individual return is required  _([Personal Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 56/2025)](https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/oman/individual/taxes-on-personal-income))_
- **Tax-free threshold (from 2028)** — OMR 42,000 of annual gross income is exempt; tax applies only above this amount OMR  _([Personal Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 56/2025)](https://www.ey.com/en_gl/technical/tax-alerts/oman-to-introduce-personal-income-tax-from-january-2028))_
- **Personal income tax rate (from 2028)** — 5% flat on annual gross income exceeding OMR 42,000 %  _([Personal Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 56/2025)](https://kpmg.com/xx/en/our-insights/gms-flash-alert/flash-alert-2025-122.html))_
- **Scope for residents (from 2028)** — Tax residents (Omanis and non-Omanis present 183+ days in a year) taxed on worldwide gross income above OMR 42,000  _([Personal Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 56/2025)](https://www.deloitte.com/middle-east/en/services/tax/perspectives/oman-personal-income-tax-law-issued.html))_
- **Individual residence test (from 2028)** — Resident if present in Oman for 183 days or more in the tax year (or an Omani citizen) (approx — confirm exact day-count rule in Executive Regulations)  _([Personal Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 56/2025)](https://www.ey.com/en_gl/technical/tax-alerts/oman-to-introduce-personal-income-tax-from-january-2028))_
- **Exempt income types (from 2028)** — Gain on sale of a primary residence, certain foreign salary, gifts, and inheritance are expected to be excluded (approx — confirm; detailed exemptions await Executive Regulations)  _([Personal Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 56/2025)](https://www.deloitte.com/middle-east/en/services/tax/perspectives/oman-personal-income-tax-law-issued.html))_
- **Deductions / reliefs (from 2028)** — The law contemplates deductions for items such as education, healthcare, housing, zakat/donations and other social allowances (approx — confirm; specifics await Executive Regulations)  _([Personal Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 56/2025)](https://www.deloitte.com/middle-east/en/services/tax/perspectives/oman-personal-income-tax-law-issued.html))_
- **Executive Regulations timing** — Detailed procedures, forms and timelines expected within one year of the law's publication (by ~30 June 2026) (approx — confirm)  _([Personal Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 56/2025)](https://kpmg.com/xx/en/our-insights/gms-flash-alert/flash-alert-2025-122.html))_
- **Non-resident individual tax (2025)** — None — non-residents pay no personal income tax on Oman-source employment income in 2025  _([Personal Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 56/2025)](https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/oman/individual/taxes-on-personal-income))_
- **Capital gains (individuals, 2025)** — No separate capital gains tax on individuals' personal investments in 2025 (approx — confirm)  _([Personal Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 56/2025)](https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/oman/individual/other-taxes))_

original_body_unit:
- **Payroll income-tax withholding (PAYE)** — None in 2025 — no income tax is withheld from salaries because Oman has no personal income tax  _(Personal Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 56/2025) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/oman/individual/taxes-on-personal-income)_
- **Social insurance scheme** — Social Protection Fund (SPF), which replaced the Public Authority for Social Insurance (PASI)  _(Social Protection Law (Royal Decree No. 52/2023) — https://www.spf.gov.om/en/faq/what-are-the-contribution-rates-to-be-paid-by-the-worker-and-employer/)_
- **Old-age, disability & death — employee share** — 7.5% of wages (Omani nationals) %  _(Social Protection Law (Royal Decree No. 52/2023) — https://www.spf.gov.om/en/faq/what-are-the-contribution-rates-to-be-paid-by-the-worker-and-employer/)_
- **Old-age, disability & death — employer share** — 11% of wages (Omani nationals) %  _(Social Protection Law (Royal Decree No. 52/2023) — https://www.spf.gov.om/en/faq/what-are-the-contribution-rates-to-be-paid-by-the-worker-and-employer/)_
- **Work injury & occupational disease — employer share** — 1% of wages (employee contributes 0%); applies to all employees including expatriates %  _(Social Protection Law (Royal Decree No. 52/2023) — https://www.spf.gov.om/en/faq/what-are-the-contribution-rates-to-be-paid-by-the-worker-and-employer/)_
- **Employment security (unemployment) — employee share** — 0.5% of wages (Omani nationals) %  _(Social Protection Law (Royal Decree No. 52/2023) — https://www.spf.gov.om/en/faq/what-are-the-contribution-rates-to-be-paid-by-the-worker-and-employer/)_
- **Employment security (unemployment) — employer share** — 0.5% of wages (Omani nationals) %  _(Social Protection Law (Royal Decree No. 52/2023) — https://www.spf.gov.om/en/faq/what-are-the-contribution-rates-to-be-paid-by-the-worker-and-employer/)_
- **Approximate combined SPF rates (Omani nationals)** — Employer ~12.5% + employee ~8% (sum of the old-age, work-injury and employment-security branches) % (approx — confirm; branch phase-in timelines vary)  _(Social Protection Law (Royal Decree No. 52/2023) — https://www.spf.gov.om/en/faq/what-are-the-contribution-rates-to-be-paid-by-the-worker-and-employer/)_
- **Expatriate employees** — Not covered by old-age/pension insurance; covered only for work-injury insurance (employer 1%) (confirm; certain branches for non-Omanis phase in later)  _(Social Protection Law (Royal Decree No. 52/2023) — https://www.spf.gov.om/en/faq/what-are-the-contribution-rates-to-be-paid-by-the-worker-and-employer/)_
- **Contribution wage base** — Calculated on the gross monthly wage (basic plus regular allowances) as defined by the SPF; subject to a contribution ceiling (approx — confirm exact wage definition and ceiling)  _(Social Protection Law (Royal Decree No. 52/2023) — https://www.spf.gov.om/en/faq/what-are-the-contribution-rates-to-be-paid-by-the-worker-and-employer/)_
- **Contribution remittance deadline** — Monthly — contributions due by the deadline set by the SPF following each month (approx — confirm exact day; commonly within the first part of the following month)  _(Social Protection Law (Royal Decree No. 52/2023) — https://www.spf.gov.om/en/faq/what-are-the-contribution-rates-to-be-paid-by-the-worker-and-employer/)_

original_section: Oman tax system at a glance (2025)
original_body_unit:
- **Standard tax year** — Calendar year (1 January – 31 December); a company may apply to use a different accounting period  _(Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 28/2009) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/oman/corporate/tax-administration)_
- **Currency** — Omani rial (OMR)  _(Central Bank of Oman)_
- **Tax authority** — Oman Tax Authority (formerly Secretariat General for Taxation)  _(Oman Tax Authority — https://tms.taxoman.gov.om/portal/tax-rate)_
- **Personal income tax (currently)** — None for tax year 2025 — Oman does not currently levy tax on individuals' employment or personal income  _(Personal Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 56/2025) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/oman/individual/taxes-on-personal-income)_
- **Personal income tax (from 2028)** — 5% on annual gross income above OMR 42,000, effective 1 January 2028 % / OMR  _(Personal Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 56/2025) — https://kpmg.com/xx/en/our-insights/gms-flash-alert/flash-alert-2025-122.html)_
- **Headline corporate income tax rate** — 15% %  _(Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 28/2009) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/oman/corporate/taxes-on-corporate-income)_
- **VAT / GST** — Yes — VAT applies at a standard rate of 5% (in force since 16 April 2021)  _(VAT Law (Royal Decree No. 121/2020) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/oman/corporate/other-taxes)_
- **Corporate residence / tax basis** — Resident companies are taxed on worldwide income; non-residents are taxed on Oman-source income (including via a permanent establishment)  _(Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 28/2009) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/oman/corporate/corporate-residence)_
- **Corporate tax return deadline** — Within 4 months of the financial year-end (annual return) (approx — confirm; sources vary between 4 and 6 months — verify against current Executive Regulations)  _(Income Tax Law (Royal Decree No. 28/2009) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/oman/corporate/tax-administration)_
- **VAT return deadline** — Quarterly — within 30 days of the end of each calendar quarter  _(VAT Law (Royal Decree No. 121/2020) — https://www.flick.network/en-om/oman-vat-registration-compliance-guide)_
- **Pillar Two / Domestic Top-up Tax** — Oman introduced a top-up tax (Income Inclusion Rule) effective 1 January 2025 for in-scope multinational groups (approx — confirm scope thresholds)  _(Top-up Tax (Royal Decree No. 70/2024))_
